properties.title: Fan two command finders out, join them, and merge through the pinned Conveyor code-review helper.
properties.workflow_source:
digraph ParallelResults {
    graph [goal="Fan two command finders out, join them, and merge through the pinned Conveyor code-review helper."]
    rankdir=LR

    start [shape=Mdiamond]
    exit  [shape=Msquare]

    // The Conveyor helper runs from the repository root and keeps its state under
    // .fabro/workflows/code-review/runtime. The workspace starts empty under
    // Petri, so this node seeds it: copy the pinned helper, then give `git
    // rev-parse HEAD` a commit to read. Signing is off so a developer's global
    // signing key is never used.
    setup [
        shape=parallelogram,
        script="mkdir -p .fabro/workflows/code-review/scripts .fabro/workflows/code-review/runtime && cp {{ inputs.helper }} .fabro/workflows/code-review/scripts/code_review.py && git init -q . && git -c commit.gpgsign=false -c user.name=petri-blackbox -c user.email=petri-blackbox@example.invalid commit -q --allow-empty -m seed && echo seeded"
    ]

    // The same hash check and prepare invocation as the Conveyor merge-node
    // graph (conveyor/.fabro/workflows/code-review/workflow.fabro, node `prepare`).
    prepare [
        shape=parallelogram,
        output_schema="routing",
        script="python3 -c \"import hashlib,sys; pairs=list(zip(sys.argv[1::2],sys.argv[2::2])); sys.exit(0 if pairs and all(hashlib.sha256(open(path,'rb').read()).hexdigest()==expected for path,expected in pairs) else 91)\" .fabro/workflows/code-review/scripts/code_review.py 58ab01ff37f0bbb7c0f94f9d634b3e5c54f66f36ea43750d81616e80b8201d3f && python3 .fabro/workflows/code-review/scripts/code_review.py prepare --level {{ inputs.level }} --target {{ inputs.target }}"
    ]

    // A command stands in for the scope agent: it writes the agent's structured
    // output under `output.scope`, where the real graph's merge_scope reads it.
    scope [
        shape=parallelogram,
        output_schema="routing",
        script="printf '%s' '{\"context_updates\":{\"output.scope\":{\"diffCommand\":\"git diff main...HEAD\",\"files\":[\"src/pager.py\",\"src/render.py\"],\"claudeMdFiles\":[],\"summary\":\"two files\",\"conventions\":\"\"}}}'"
    ]
    merge_scope [
        shape=parallelogram,
        stdin_source="context.output.scope",
        script="python3 .fabro/workflows/code-review/scripts/code_review.py merge scope",
        output_schema="routing"
    ]

    // Two finders, each a command in place of the review agent. Each writes a
    // distinct candidate under the same context key `output.finder`.
    find [shape=component, label="Finders"]
    finder_a [
        shape=parallelogram,
        output_schema="routing",
        script="printf '%s' '{\"context_updates\":{\"output.finder\":{\"candidates\":[{\"file\":\"src/pager.py\",\"line\":12,\"summary\":\"page_count drops the final partial page\",\"failure_scenario\":\"7 items with page size 3 reports 2 pages, so item 7 is unreachable\"}]}}}'"
    ]
    finder_b [
        shape=parallelogram,
        output_schema="routing",
        script="printf '%s' '{\"context_updates\":{\"output.finder\":{\"candidates\":[{\"file\":\"src/render.py\",\"line\":40,\"summary\":\"render escapes the title twice\",\"failure_scenario\":\"a title containing & renders as &amp;\"}]}}}'"
    ]
    find_join [shape=tripleoctagon, label="Gather finder candidates"]
    merge_find [
        shape=parallelogram,
        stdin_source="context.parallel.results",
        script="python3 .fabro/workflows/code-review/scripts/code_review.py merge find",
        output_schema="routing"
    ]
    verify_gate [shape=diamond, label="Any candidates to verify?"]

    // Two verifiers, one per pooled location, in the order merge_find grouped them.
    verify [shape=component, label="Verify locations"]
    verifier_a [
        shape=parallelogram,
        output_schema="routing",
        script="printf '%s' '{\"context_updates\":{\"output.verifier\":{\"verdicts\":[{\"index\":0,\"verdict\":\"CONFIRMED\",\"evidence\":\"page_count uses floor division\"}]}}}'"
    ]
    verifier_b [
        shape=parallelogram,
        output_schema="routing",
        script="printf '%s' '{\"context_updates\":{\"output.verifier\":{\"verdicts\":[{\"index\":0,\"verdict\":\"PLAUSIBLE\",\"evidence\":\"escape is called in two layers\"}]}}}'"
    ]
    verify_join [shape=tripleoctagon, label="Gather verdicts"]
    merge_verify [
        shape=parallelogram,
        stdin_source="context.parallel.results",
        script="python3 .fabro/workflows/code-review/scripts/code_review.py merge verify",
        output_schema="routing"
    ]

    tally [
        shape=parallelogram,
        script="python3 .fabro/workflows/code-review/scripts/code_review.py tally",
        output_schema="routing"
    ]
    finalize [
        shape=parallelogram,
        script="python3 .fabro/workflows/code-review/scripts/code_review.py finalize",
        output_schema="routing"
    ]
    // The workspace does not outlive the run, so the report is read back into
    // the command output where the harness can see it.
    report [
        shape=parallelogram,
        script="cat .fabro/workflows/code-review/runtime/report.md"
    ]

    start -> setup -> prepare -> scope -> merge_scope -> find
    find -> finder_a
    find -> finder_b
    finder_a -> find_join
    finder_b -> find_join
    find_join -> merge_find -> verify_gate
    verify_gate -> verify [condition="context.run_verify=true"]
    verify_gate -> tally
    verify -> verifier_a
    verify -> verifier_b
    verifier_a -> verify_join
    verifier_b -> verify_join
    verify_join -> merge_verify -> tally
    tally -> finalize -> report -> exit
}

finder_jobs.assignment:
Run the diff command recorded in the review scope and review ONLY through the lens of your assigned angle:

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

Surface up to 6 candidate findings.
finder_jobs.label: angle-A

finder_jobs.assignment:
Run the diff command recorded in the review scope and review ONLY through the lens of your assigned angle:

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

Surface up to 6 candidate findings.
finder_jobs.label: angle-B

finder_jobs.assignment:
Run the diff command recorded in the review scope and review ONLY through the lens of your assigned angle:

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

Surface up to 6 candidate findings.
finder_jobs.label: angle-C

finder_jobs.assignment:
Run the diff command recorded in the review scope and review through EACH of the following cleanup lenses:

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.


### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.


### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.


### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.


### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Surface up to 30 candidate findings. Cover whichever lenses apply — you do not need findings from every lens; prioritize the highest-cost issues across all of them.
finder_jobs.label: cleanup

Run the diff command recorded in the review scope and review through EACH of the following cleanup lenses:

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.


### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.


### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.


### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.
